speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mucosal Impaction (Bezoar) or Gastric Outlet Obstruction secondary to chronic alcoholism and recent retching, causing aspiration and chest pain. The history of persistent vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption followed by choking and chest pain is highly suggestive of gastric contents or a foreign body causing obstruction and subsequent aspiration. Immediate endoscopy is required to visualize and remove the obstruction.
